title: Flat internal modules under inverse image and coefficient isomorphism
statement: Use [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. For any morphism f:X→Y of schemes, commutative monoid objects R and S in abelian sheaves on the pro-étale sites of Y and X respectively, and a monoid isomorphism ρ:S→f*R, the functor Mod.mapModComap ρ, namely ambient inverse image on internal R-modules followed by restriction along ρ, preserves flat objects. Flat means exactness of tensoring with the module, in the internal module category. No finiteness, Noetherian, or flatness assumption on a residue quotient is required.

proof.text: Use the explicit balanced tensor comparison to identify internal flatness with IsFlatOnSite of section modules. The comparison and its inverse are constructed and proved in Lean by the universal properties of tensor products, coequalizers and sheafification.

Construct the set inverse-image L and its right adjoint from pro-etale base change. Filtered colimits of types commute with finite limits; the general flat-functor Kan-extension theorem gives left exactness of L. Identify the transported internal module functor with an algebraic inverse image over this concrete L.

Apply preservation of flatness for AlgebraicInverseImageOfUniverses to the source section module. Transfer the result through the module-functor comparison and the source equivalence unit. IsFlatOnSite is invariant under module isomorphism: map each finite relation across the isomorphism, take a local matrix factorization, and map its witness sections back. Finally apply the reverse internal/section flatness comparison.

proof_origin.note: C2: explicit internal/section tensor comparison and the proved universe-polymorphic algebraic inverse-image flatness theorem; only the geometric algebraic-operations identification remains split off.
